subject: Sprint gating: HW sourcing alignment for NDX-4791
messages:
From: Peter Shaw <peter.shaw@oemtech.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus AI - Ops Team <ops@nimbus.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OEM quote & sprint gating — initial availability windows (attached)

Hi Grace / team,

Attached is OEM quote v3 and the manufacturing window breakdown. Key points:
- Lead time: current queue puts metal allocation at ~14–18 weeks from PO for the first tranche; second tranche adds ~8–10 weeks after that depending on chassis availability.
- Shipping: partial shipments are possible (min 30% per shipment) but incur a split-shipment fee we detail in the quote.
- Custom SKUs: certain custom cooling options add an additional 3–4 weeks.

Given NDX-4791’s requested onramp (production traffic in Q4), we recommend locking tranche sizes and PO timing this week so we can secure the July manufacturing band. If you confirm a tranche schedule (quantities + desired arrive-by windows), we’ll hold slots and produce an updated shipping plan.

Attachments: oem_quote_v3.pdf (quote + ETA table), manufacturing_gantt.png (inline in PDF)

Questions for you:
1) Can Redwood accept a two-tranche PO (50 nodes / 150 nodes) with the understanding the second tranche is contingent on chassis allocation?
2) If Redwood needs a cloud backstop, we can coordinate a short-term reserved capacity credit through our partner Nimbus; let us know if you want that option priced.

I can jump on a 30-min sync tomorrow afternoon if useful.

—Peter
Peter Shaw
OEM Sales Director | OEMTech Systems
peter.shaw@oemtech.com
+1 (415) 555-0182
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Peter Shaw <peter.shaw@oemtech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OEM quote & sprint gating — initial availability windows (attached)

Thanks Peter — helpful detail. Quick summary / asks from our side: 

- Deal constraints: NDX-4791 has a hard production target in early Q4; we need a reliable first-tranche delivery by mid-September to start internal integration.
- Proposed tranche plan (tentative): 50 nodes (sept target) / 150 nodes (nov target). Can you confirm whether the 14–18 week band maps to that first-tranche Sept window if we PO this week?
- Nimbus mismatch: Nimbus has signaled reserved capacity for the same customer starting in Oct; we need clarity on whether OEM partial shipping + Nimbus backfill is a viable hybrid route. Please confirm lead timing if partial shipments occur.

Action items: 
- Peter: confirm PO-to-ship ETA for the 50-node tranche if PO issued today; update the attached capacity spreadsheet to include per-chassis ETA (we'll use nimbus_capacity_matrix.xlsx as the merge target).
- Ben: confirm procurement budget carve-out and whether we can accept split-shipment fees (figure needed to sign PO).
- Karthik: flag any constraints from our Dedicated pool provisioning (network stacks, rack density) that would affect acceptance windows.

I’m attaching our internal planning doc (redwood_capacity_playbook.md) so you see our acceptance SLA and customs handling notes. If we can get a firm ETA by EOD Wednesday I’ll escalate to the deal sponsor and lock the tranche.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Capacity & Onboarding | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Peter Shaw <peter.shaw@oemtech.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OEM quote & sprint gating — initial availability windows (attached)

Agree with Grace. Budget note: we have a reserved carve-out for Q4 on NDX-4791 but we need line-item clarity on the split-shipment fee and any holdback for customs/insurance. Please include estimated fees in the updated quote.

From procurement perspective I need:
- Firm delivery windows (calendar dates) tied to each shipment tranche
- Documented penalty language or credit if OEM misses the agreed ship window by >7 calendar days
- ALS (accepted logistics statement) confirming min qty per pallet and whether pallet consolidation is possible to reduce freight.

Lauren — can you flag if Legal needs to push any changes on the penalty language before I approve the PO?

Ben Carter
Senior Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Peter Shaw <peter.shaw@oemtech.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Nimbus AI - Ops Team <ops@nimbus.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Jul 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OEM quote & sprint gating — initial availability windows (attached)

Thanks — looping back with updated detail (see attached schedule). 

Quick answers inline: 
- If PO received today we can commit the first tranche to a ship date of Sep 12–18 (14 weeks after PO), subject to customs hold variations. Second tranche (remaining 150 nodes) can be scheduled for Nov 7–15; that schedule assumes chassis allocation confirmation next week.
- Split-shipment fee: estimate $3,200 for the 50/150 split; we can reduce to $2,000 if you accept consolidated packaging (adds ~4 days).
- Penalty language: OEMTech can accept a limited credit schedule (0.5% of tranche value per week late, capped at 4%) — I'll have Legal draft exact wording.
- Nimbus backfill: confirmed — Nimbus Ops can provision reserved cloud capacity starting Oct 1 for up to 90 days while hardware is staged. Ops (cc'd) will follow up with a credit estimate to mirror your unit economics.

Attachments: oem_quote_v3.pdf (revised with fees), shipping_plan_ndx4791.xlsx (ETA by chassis + HS codes)

Please confirm if the Sep 12–18 window is acceptable and whether Redwood wants the consolidated-packaging option to reduce fees. Upon confirmation we will generate a formal PO-ready invoice and manufacturing hold.
